items.topic: GERD — elevate head of bed; avoid lying down soon after eating
items.stem: An older adult with GERD asks how to reduce nighttime heartburn. Which teaching point is most appropriate?

options.text: Raise the head of the bed and avoid lying down for several hours after eating
Lie flat immediately after large evening meals to promote digestion
Place pillows under the knees only; head-of-bed elevation never helps reflux
Skip all lifestyle measures because only surgery treats GERD

rationales.A: Correct. Merck Treatment of GERD: elevate head of bed; limit food within 4 hours of bedtime. MedlinePlus: raise head of bed; avoid lying down 2–3 hours after eating.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Lying down soon after eating worsens reflux (MedlinePlus/Merck).
rationales.C: Incorrect. Head-of-bed elevation is a standard nonpharmacologic measure.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Most people manage GERD with lifestyle changes and medicines; surgery is uncommon first-line.

items.topic: NGN matrix — GERD lifestyle teaching indicated vs not
items.stem: For an older adult with uncomplicated GERD, indicate whether each teaching point is Indicated or Not indicated.

rows.text: Elevate the head of the bed for sleep (blocks or wedge)
Avoid lying down for about 2–3 hours after meals
Lie flat right after a large bedtime snack to settle the stomach
Consider weight loss and smoking cessation when appropriate
Tell the client lifestyle measures never matter if antacids are available

rationales.R1: Indicated. Merck and MedlinePlus support raising the head of the bed.
rationales.R2: Indicated. MedlinePlus: avoid lying down for at least 2–3 hours after eating; Merck: limit food near bedtime.
rationales.R3: Not indicated. Lying flat soon after eating worsens reflux.
rationales.R4: Indicated. Both sources list weight loss and smoking cessation when appropriate.
rationales.R5: Not indicated. Lifestyle modification is first-line nonpharmacologic care alongside acid suppression when needed.

items.topic: Chronic venous insufficiency — elevate legs and use compression
items.stem: An older adult with chronic venous insufficiency has dependent leg edema. Which self-care instruction is most appropriate?

options.text: Elevate the legs periodically and use prescribed compression stockings
Keep the legs dangling dependent all day to improve arterial inflow
Avoid compression because stockings always worsen venous edema
Never change position; prolonged standing is preferred therapy

rationales.A: Correct. Merck: elevate legs above the right atrium ≥3 times/day for ≥30 minutes; compression is recommended. OpenStax: compression stockings and elevating legs assist venous return.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Dependent dangling worsens venous pooling/edema.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Compression is a mainstay of CVI treatment.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Prolonged standing worsens symptoms; position changes are encouraged.

sources.title: Chronic Venous Insufficiency and Post-Thrombotic Syndrome
sources.evidence: Elevate leg above right atrium ≥3×/day ≥30 min; compression recommended for edema/ulcers.

sources.section: Venous Insufficiency: Clinical Manifestations and Nursing Care
sources.evidence: Wear compression stockings; rest and elevate legs; change positions to avoid prolonged standing.

items.topic: Phenytoin — gingival hyperplasia; emphasize oral hygiene
items.stem: A client starting long-term phenytoin asks about mouth care. Which teaching is most accurate?

options.text: Phenytoin can cause gum overgrowth; good oral hygiene and dental follow-up help reduce gum damage
Phenytoin never affects the gums, so toothbrushing can be skipped
Mouth care is unnecessary because phenytoin sterilizes the oral cavity
Clients should stop all dental visits while taking phenytoin

rationales.A: Correct. OpenStax: long-term hydantoins (phenytoin) can cause gingival hyperplasia. MedlinePlus: care for teeth/gums/mouth is very important to decrease gum damage risk.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Gingival hyperplasia is a recognized long-term effect.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Phenytoin does not sterilize the mouth; oral care remains essential.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Dental awareness/follow-up supports gum health during therapy.

items.topic: Fentanyl patch — do not cut; avoid external heat over the patch
items.stem: A client with a fentanyl transdermal patch asks about home safety. Which instruction is most important?

options.text: Do not cut or alter the patch, and avoid heating pads or other direct external heat over the application site
Cut the patch in half if pain is mild so the dose is smaller
Apply a heating pad over the patch to speed pain relief
Hot tubs and electric blankets over the patch are encouraged

rationales.A: Correct. Health Canada Sandoz PM: do not use if altered/cut/damaged; avoid direct external heat (heating pads, electric blankets, saunas, etc.). NCBI Open RN: never apply heat over fentanyl patches—increases release and can cause overdose.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Cutting/altering the patch is contraindicated and unsafe.
rationales.C: Incorrect. External heat increases absorption and overdose risk.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Hot whirlpool/sauna/electric blankets are listed heat sources to avoid.

items.topic: Allopurinol — stop immediately and seek care for rash (SJS/TEN risk)
items.stem: A client taking allopurinol for gout develops a new widespread itchy rash. What is the priority teaching action?

options.text: Stop allopurinol immediately and seek urgent medical care because rash may precede severe hypersensitivity reactions
Double the next dose to treat the rash as a gout flare
Continue allopurinol and ignore any skin changes
Apply a heating pad to the rash and keep taking the tablets

rationales.A: Correct. Health Canada Apo-Allopurinol PM: discontinue immediately at appearance of skin rash—may progress to SJS/TEN/DRESS. MedlinePlus: stop and call doctor/get emergency care for rash, itching, hives, blistering.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Dose increase is dangerous with possible hypersensitivity; stop the drug.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Rash requires immediate stop and evaluation.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Heat/rash self-treatment does not address hypersensitivity risk.

B1.text: stop the medicine and seek care immediately
take an extra dose and wait a week
crush all tablets into juice for better absorption

B3.text: drink plenty of fluids (e.g., about eight 240 mL cups of water/liquids unless directed otherwise)
avoid all oral fluids for 24 hours after each dose
replace water with only grapefruit juice
restrict fluids to one sip per day

rationales.B3b: Incorrect. Fluid restriction is not the teaching.
rationales.B3c: Incorrect. Not the recommended hydration teaching.
rationales.B3d: Incorrect. Inadequate fluids contradict MedlinePlus guidance.

items.topic: Adult ear drops — pull auricle/pinna up and back to straighten canal
items.stem: The nurse prepares to instill prescribed otic drops for an adult client. How should the nurse straighten the ear canal?

options.text: Gently pull the auricle (pinna) upward and backward
Pull the auricle firmly downward and forward only
Never touch the pinna; insert the dropper deep into the middle ear
Pull both earlobes toward the nose simultaneously

rationales.A: Correct. OpenStax: for an adult, pull the auricle up and back. MedlinePlus: pull the ear backward and upward (adult).
rationales.B: Incorrect. Down-and-back is the pediatric/young-child technique, not the adult default.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Dropper should not be forced deep; tip should stay clean and not traumatize the canal.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Not a recommended canal-straightening method.

should be cut in half for milder pain
should be microwaved to activate the drug
must be chewed before skin placement

B2.text: avoid heating pads, electric blankets, saunas, and hot whirlpool baths over the site
apply a heating pad continuously over the patch
sunbathe with the patch uncovered for better effect
soak in a hot tub with the patch each hour

rationales.B3a: Correct. HC PM/NCBI: heat increases release/absorption and can cause overdose/death.
rationales.B3b: Incorrect. Heat increases, not inactivates, delivery.
